newsitem.title: UK: Europe Feb equity mutual fund inflows jump -- report.
newsitem.headline: Europe Feb equity mutual fund inflows jump -- report.

text.p: Net inflows into European equity mutual funds rose to their highest level since January 1994 in February, hitting $5 billion from under $4 billion in January, JP Morgan said in a report on global fund flows.
It said Germany, Sweden, Spain and the UK saw particularly large flows into equities.

In Germany, net subscriptions rose 38 percent month-on-month to 3.7 billion marks. In the UK they topped one billion stg to hit a fresh record, and the report said this was most likely due to seasonal factors ahead of the end of the tax year in April.
In Spain, it estimated flows into equities in February rose 53 percent from January.
French and Italian flows into domestic equities were lighter than in the previous month but there were strong flows into international funds, particularly those focused on Europe.

The report said that in Germany some 754 million marks the 3.7 billion marks of net subscriptions into equity funds went to domestic shares. But, including the domestic equity component of mixed funds, it said total flows into German shares were close to 3.2 billion marks, their highest level since January 1994.
German equities accounted for a record 23.2 percent of portfolios at the end of January.
Net subscriptions to international equities rose sharply, attracting some 3.5 billion marks in equity funds alone. Bond funds attracted 4.8 billion marks.

JP Morgan said the one billion stg inflow into UK equities confirmed a renewed enthusiasm for domestic equities from both retail and institutional investors, with UK growth sectors again attracting the bulk of new equity fund investment.
Net subscriptions to international equities rose to 192 million stg after pausing in January, with 63 percent directed at European equities.
Institutional investors showed strong interest in global emerging markets, it said.

Overall. net subscriptions to all funds in the UK rose to 1.4 billion stg, with domestic equities accounting for some 54.2 percent of portfolio assets, while foreign equities declined to 39 percent -- its lowest share since January 1992.

French flows saw modest domestic equity inflows, confirming some retail interest in domestic shares, but the main beneficiaries of equity fund inflows were international equity SICAVs, attracting a net 1.3 billion francs.
This showed an 86 percent rise on January to its highest level since March 1994, and was again concentrated on European equities.
Some 1.9 billion francs flowed into fixed income SICAVs, representing the first net subscription to the sector in three years.
In Italy. net flows into domestic equities were surprisingly low, reflecting caution from retail investors. But it said fund managers were less cautious.
New equity investment was mostly directed at international equities, with Europe and emerging markets the two most popular sectors.
Bond flows were strong with net subscriptions at 12.09 billion lira ($7.1 billion). Long term instruments attracted the most interest.

Net flows into Spanish equities through mixed and equity funds rose some 53 percent month-on-month to 255 billion pesetas, it estimated. In total, Spanish mutual funds attracted a net 1.2 trillion pesetas in February.

Swedish domestic and international equity funds saw strong subscriptions in February of eight billion crowns. Flows to mixed funds were also strong at 1.8 billion crowns, but fixed income funds eased to 520 million.
-- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887
